title: A wider position uncertainty
hook: Change position uncertainty and predict minimum momentum-uncertainty bound.
misconception: minimum momentum-uncertainty bound doubles when position uncertainty doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply Δp ≥ ħ/(2Δx) to compare minimum momentum-uncertainty bound when position uncertainty changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With the Heisenberg uncertainty relation for positive uncertainties, Δp ≥ ħ/(2Δx). When position uncertainty doubles, minimum momentum-uncertainty bound becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Δp ≥ ħ/(2Δx); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider the Heisenberg uncertainty relation for positive uncertainties, with a nonzero initial result. If position uncertainty triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on minimum momentum-uncertainty bound?
recall.why: Apply Δp ≥ ħ/(2Δx) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
